flags.observation: The badger drums alone while "the brain cannot generate" the rhythm, a clear in-world claim distinct from the other organ voices.
The Semmelweis Problem is stated by an unnamed sign on a barn door, the only card not voiced by an animal or figure.
The Blind Eye addresses "you" directly mid-sequence, shifting from organ-report mode into direct audience commentary.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" arrives right after a body-keeps-the-score closing, a tonal jump from philosophical to sign-off.
The archive transition line names no specific figure, reading more generic next to the vivid animal personifications around it.

fractalCards.observation: Each organ is voiced by its own figure making claims about itself, such as the gut subway line "The subway runs the city."

individuality.observation: Specific inventions like the badger drumming alone, the crab "with a fortress on its back", and "The Semmelweis Problem" avoid generic body-trivia listing.

outro.observation: "Listen to the drum" closes the drum/heart motif, but "Stay Fluffy, Folks!" lands as a separate sign-off tag that breaks the register right after.

performer.observation: The voice is dry and self-doubting, unsure if anyone is present ("Or nobody did, and I am talking to my own pipes"), then fiercely possessive about breath ("In. Out. Mine.").

resident.observation: The piece opens and closes inside its own cockpit, addressing whoever climbed in, consistent with a figure performing in its own home space.

standalone.observation: The cockpit/colossus conceit and the City Inside premise are established in the first four beats, giving newcomers full context before any organ speaks.

storyBetweenCards.observation: Reports escalate from calm organ check-ins (heart, lungs, liver, gut) to sirens and immune warfare, then pivot to a historical argument over authorship before landing on free will.

transferable.observation: The content is organ-specific (heart, lungs, liver, gut, immune system, named historical physicians) and could not move to another topic without full new material.

lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

Somebody climbed into my cockpit again. Or nobody did, and I am talking to my own pipes. Either way, keep your hands off the levers. They are painted on.

I am a colossus, a whole metropolis on two legs. I walk, I fight, I hold very still for statues. I have not once decided anything.

Look through the hatch. The City Inside has been running the civilization while you were busy with other things.

Turns out that means me. The Citizen: you never once told this city what to do. It never once asked your permission.

The intercom crackles. The departments report whether I ask or not.

Cardiac, down in the boiler room, a badger on a drum kit: The Heart: the brain can modify the rate. The brain cannot generate it. The badger drums alone.

Deck two, two broccoli trees trading birds: The Lungs: seventy square meters folded into your chest, the only manual override. That one I get to touch. In. Out. Mine.

A grim beaver at the oil drums, does not look up: The Liver: Prometheus was anatomically correct. It's the only organ that grows back.

The subway, full of commuters who do not get off: The Gut: eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city.

At night the mice come out with mops. The Night Shift: sleep is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.

Then the sirens. The rats in riot gear take the intercom.

The Immune System: a library of every murder attempt. It remembers things you have forgotten.

The spider in the copy room answers for the typos: DNA Replication: one error per billion letters; you have had cancer, the spider usually eats it.

Then a voice from the shoreline, a crab with a fortress on its back: Cancer: evolution occurring inside you. It is not a disease; it is a competitor.

And my firefighters, with flamethrowers: Inflammation: the response that heals the wound becomes the mechanism that burns the city.

The dog in the corner bites his tail. Autoimmune: the discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine, pointed the wrong way.

In the archive, old voices argue about who drew my blueprints.

A mole in a ruff, stomping on a textbook: Andreas Vesalius looked at the body instead of the book. Everyone else was wrong.

A raccoon washing his hands while the shadows laugh: Ignaz Semmelweis saved the mothers. The doctors committed him. He died of the infection.

And the barn door with the big sign on it: The Semmelweis Problem: evidence available, implication uncomfortable, we reject the finding.

The tortoise with four potions still thinks he built me. The Humoralist: wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.

About you, by the way. The Blind Eye: you have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses. So if nobody is really standing there, I have painted you in.

Last report, from the owls upstairs in their judge wigs: The Brain: the decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it.

You are the press secretary, not the president.

Half a second. When I hold still for a statue, somebody else already picked the pose.

The Scorekeeper: the body keeps the score because the body is the score.

Every colossus in every square thinks it is marching. Most of us are being marched by a badger with a drum.

So whoever climbed in: leave the levers. Listen to the drum.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

styleA: Tight seventies funk at 104 BPM with a machine pulse: clavinet riffs, choppy wah guitar, slap bass, dry drums with a steady kick like heavy footsteps, three-piece horn stabs, hissing hi-hat. One deep male baritone, unhurried and a little metallic, talking close to the mic, surprised by his own lines. Punchy analog mix; sudden stops where only bass and kick keep walking.
styleB: Big beat at 122 BPM: chopped breakbeat drums, distorted acid bassline, sampled brass hits, clanking metal percussion, rising filter sweeps. One deadpan male voice with a thin radio filter on the asides. Loud compressed mix, hard cuts to silence before each new section.
